description: Operational testing objectives and testability requirements for a service (SE-02-A09)

testability_requirements.description: Architectural features that enable operational testing

checks: Dependencies optional (don't check DB, message queue)

readiness_check.response: 200 OK if service is ready (dependencies healthy)

distributed_tracing.propagation: Trace context propagated via HTTP headers

configuration_validation.fail_fast: Service exits with non-zero code if invalid configuration

test_mode.behavior: Use in-memory database, stub external APIs, disable background jobs

mock_dependencies.approach: Dependency injection allows replacing real clients with mocks

deterministic_behavior.random_seed: Accept RANDOM_SEED environment variable for reproducible tests
deterministic_behavior.timestamps: Accept FIXED_TIME environment variable for time-dependent tests
deterministic_behavior.external_ids: Use predictable IDs in test mode (sequential, not UUIDs)

graceful_degradation.database_unavailable: Return 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After header
graceful_degradation.external_api_down: Use circuit breaker, return cached data or default values
graceful_degradation.rate_limited: Return 429 Too Many Requests with rate limit info in headers

deployment_test_scenarios.description: Tests to validate deployment configuration, not business logic

scenarios.test: Service starts successfully with production-like configuration
steps: Start container with production environment variables
Wait up to 30 seconds for service to initialize
Check /health endpoint returns 200 OK
Check logs for startup completion message
scenarios.success_criteria: Container starts, health endpoint responds 200 OK within 30s, no ERROR logs

scenarios.test: Service connects to database with correct permissions
steps: Start database container with service user credentials (not postgres superuser)
Start service container with DATABASE_URL pointing to service database
Check service connects to database
Run migrations as service user
Verify migrations create tables successfully
Check service can SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
scenarios.success_criteria: Connection established, migrations run successfully as service user, CRUD operations work
failure_modes: Permission denied (service user lacks CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE)
Connection refused (wrong host, port, or credentials)
CRUD operations fail (missing SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE permissions)

steps: Start service without database
Check service starts but /ready returns 503
Check /health still returns 200 (service running, dependencies not required for health)
Check logs show clear error about missing database
Start database
Wait for service to detect database (circuit breaker retry)
Check /ready now returns 200
scenarios.success_criteria: Circuit breaker trips, service returns 503 with clear error message, recovers when dependency available
failure_modes: Service crashes instead of handling missing dependency
No clear error message (generic 'Internal Server Error')
Circuit breaker never recovers when dependency returns

scenarios.test: Service validates configuration at startup and fails fast with actionable error
steps: Start service with invalid DATABASE_URL (wrong format)
Check service exits immediately with non-zero code
Check logs show specific validation error (not generic crash)
Fix configuration
Start service again
Check service starts successfully
scenarios.success_criteria: Invalid config detected, service fails fast with actionable error message
failure_modes: Service starts with invalid config, crashes later
Generic error message (not specific to configuration problem)

steps: Start service with resource limits (e.g., --memory=512m --cpus=1.0)
Send load to service (e.g., 100 req/sec for 1 minute)
Monitor memory usage
Check memory stays within limit (no OOMKilled)
Check service continues responding
scenarios.success_criteria: Container stays within limits (< 512MB RAM, < 100% CPU), service responsive under load

operational_acceptance_criteria.description: Criteria for service to be considered deployment-ready

criteria.target: < 30 seconds from container start to health check passing
criteria.rationale: Fast startup enables rapid scaling and recovery
criteria.measurement: Time from docker run to first successful /health 200 OK

criteria.rationale: Orchestrators need fast health checks for rapid failure detection
criteria.measurement: p95 latency of /health endpoint under no load

criteria.rationale: Readiness checks can be slower (check dependencies) but must be responsive
criteria.measurement: p95 latency of /ready endpoint under no load

criteria.target: Completes in-flight requests within 30s on SIGTERM
criteria.measurement: Send SIGTERM, verify no requests fail, all complete within 30s

criteria.target: Automatic restart and recovery without manual intervention
criteria.measurement: Kill service process, verify orchestrator restarts it, service recovers automatically

criteria.target: No ERROR or WARNING logs during normal startup
criteria.rationale: Clean logs indicate proper configuration and dependencies
criteria.measurement: Review logs from container start to /ready 200 OK, count ERROR/WARNING

smoke_test_requirements.description: Fast tests (< 30s total) to validate basic functionality after deployment
smoke_test_requirements.total_time_budget: < 30 seconds for all smoke tests combined

tests.what: Create, read, update, delete primary entities
tests.purpose: Verify core business logic works and database is operational
tests.success_criteria: All CRUD operations return expected status codes (201, 200, 200, 204)

tests.what: Valid token accepted, invalid token rejected
tests.example: GET /api/protected with valid JWT → 200 OK, GET /api/protected without token → 401 Unauthorized
tests.success_criteria: Valid token accepted, invalid token rejected with 401

tests.purpose: Verify database setup correct and migrations ran
tests.example: SELECT version FROM schema_migrations → verify latest migration applied
tests.success_criteria: Latest migration version present in database

tests.what: Service can call dependencies and handle responses
tests.example: Call API endpoint that triggers call to another service, verify response includes data from dependency
tests.success_criteria: Service successfully calls dependency, receives response, returns expected result

tests.what: Service returns appropriate error for invalid input
tests.purpose: Verify validation and error handling work
tests.example: POST /api/entities with invalid payload → 400 Bad Request with validation errors
tests.success_criteria: Invalid input rejected with 400 and descriptive error message

service_architecture.relationship: Testability requirements from this document become implementation requirements in service architecture

risk_assessment.relationship: High-risk services (score >= 2.6) require more comprehensive operational testing objectives

d_06_5_validation.relationship: D-06.5 pre-deployment validation uses these objectives to validate service before operational testing

system_test_strategy.relationship: System test strategy aggregates operational testing objectives from all services

llm_agent_guidance.customization: Customize testability requirements, deployment scenarios, and acceptance criteria based on service complexity and risk level
llm_agent_guidance.high_risk_services: High-risk services (score >= 2.6 from risk_assessment.json) need more comprehensive deployment scenarios and stricter acceptance criteria
llm_agent_guidance.framework_specific: Health endpoints (/health, /ready) apply to UAF services; other frameworks may use different testability mechanisms (e.g., observable state variables for biological systems)
llm_agent_guidance.smoke_tests: Smoke tests must be fast (< 30s total) - they run after every deployment in D-06.5 and operational testing
llm_agent_guidance.fail_fast: Configuration validation should fail fast at startup, not crash later at runtime
llm_agent_guidance.production_ready: Operational acceptance criteria define 'production ready' - all must be met before operational testing

metadata.usage: Used by SE-02-A09 during service architecture specification
